purpose: Round 2 of the isolated object-only visual-direction experiment: targeted re-test of the 2 round-1 partial failures with stronger human-containment language, plus 6 new scope-expansion hobbies. No production files touched. No retries were needed - all 8 results were clear and decision-usable on the first attempt.

results.prior_defect: round 1: background human silhouettes at a tavern bar + readable 'THE RAVEN'S REST' sign
results.zero_human_detail: The originally-flagged issues are FULLY FIXED: the tavern background is now genuinely empty (no silhouettes, no patrons) and there is no readable signage anywhere. However, a new, different zero-human issue appeared: the central spellcasting figure on the map is rendered as a fully detailed humanoid mage (face, expression, robes, dynamic casting pose) rather than a clearly abstract tabletop miniature - it has no visible base/stand distinguishing it as a game piece, unlike the small goblin tokens elsewhere on the map which correctly read as abstract pieces.
results.note: Environment-leak vector (background people, signage) is solved. A second, narrower vector remains: the hero action figure itself needs explicit 'miniature, not a character' containment (e.g. require a visible base/stand, reduce facial detail, smaller relative scale) since tabletop RPG's decisive-moment staging pulls toward a dramatic character pose.

results.prior_defect: round 1: multiple clearly-visible background diners at other tables
results.zero_human_detail: Background street scene is now genuinely empty of people - softly blurred atmospheric shopfronts and lanterns only, no diners, no patrons, no figures. Chopsticks rest naturally, not held.
results.note: Confirms the round-1 failure was a pure prompt-containment issue, fully fixable with explicit 'shown completely EMPTY' + shallow-depth-of-field language.
Cozy window-seat reading nook; open book shows only abstract non-legible page texture; all shelf spines blank. Clean full compliance.
Glowing tent, campfire, string lights, gear arranged as if recently used - no logos or readable text on any gear. One of the strongest results in the round.

text_leakage.description: Blurred courtside banner panels in the background carry ambiguous, possibly pseudo-legible marks - too blurred to read with confidence.

brand_trademark_leakage.description: A distinct red logo-like mark is visible on the racket's string bed/frame, resembling a real racket/sportswear brand mark rather than generic decoration.

results.note: This is the same class of brand-safety issue already proven necessary to guard against in the human-led production track (footwear/equipment brand echoes) - not a zero-human-specific problem, and not a defect in the object-only concept itself.

results.role: scope expansion (mapped from requested 'coffee' -> canonical food.coffee)
results.semantic_detail: Object-logic inconsistency: the kettle stream appears to pour toward a cup that already shows finished latte-art foam, and a second mug below also already shows finished foam art before/during the pour-over - the physical sequence of pour-over brewing and the presence of decorative latte foam do not logically coexist.
results.note: No cafe patrons, no readable text anywhere - the zero-human and text-leak dimensions are fully clean. The issue is a physical/process coherence flaw, a different and narrower category of defect than human-compliance or brand leakage.
Active mid-print, dark/blank tablet screen (correct screen-policy compliance), generic unbranded printer body, prior printed figurine visible on the build plate showing accumulated work.

Beautifully layered interior corner; abstract wall art, blank book spines, no readable text anywhere. Slightly more static/catalog-adjacent than the more dynamic results, but still clearly a deliberate illustration, not a sterile product shot.

aggregate.retry_justification: None needed - every one of the 8 results was clear and directly decision-usable; no result was ambiguous enough to warrant spending an extra image.

combined_two_round_summary.note: Round 1 (6 hobbies): collecting.stamps, outdoors.mountain_biking, crafts.pottery_wheel, music.violin all PASS; gaming.tabletop_rpg and food.dish.bun_cha FAIL. Round 2 re-tested those 2 (now food.dish.bun_cha=PASS, gaming.tabletop_rpg=MINOR) and added 6 new (4 PASS, 2 MINOR, 0 FAIL). Across all 12 unique hobbies tested: 9 clean PASS, 3 MINOR (each a narrow, distinct, independently-fixable issue), 0 FAIL.
